record.original_question: For higher-rank unitary perturbations, determine which parts of Aronszajn-Donoghue theory survive after the necessary modifications from the rank-one setting, especially when scalar spectral measures are replaced by vector-valued measures.

evidence.quote: Open direction: In the case of higher rank perturbations, we certainly cannot hope that the singular parts of two perturbed operators’ spectral measures are mutually singular.

However, it would be interesting to see how much of Aronszajn–Donoghue theory can still be true with appropriate changes in the statements. For example, instead of the scalar spectral measure, one would need to consider vector-valued measures.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $U_0$ be a unitary operator on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and let $\{U_\gamma\}$ be a family of finite-rank unitary perturbations of $U_0$ (for example, the Aleksandrov–Clark family obtained from a fixed $d$-dimensional subspace, parametrized by unitary $d\times d$ matrices $\gamma$). For each $\gamma$, let $M_\gamma$ denote the associated matrix-valued (operator-valued) spectral measure on the unit circle $\mathbb T$ taken with respect to a fixed cyclic family of $d$ vectors, and write its Lebesgue decomposition $M_\gamma = M_\gamma^{ac} + M_\gamma^{s}$ into absolutely continuous and singular parts (with respect to normalized Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb T$).

Recall the rank-one Aronszajn–Donoghue theorem: when $d=1$ and $U_0,U_\gamma$ differ by a rank-one unitary perturbation with cyclic vector, the singular parts of the scalar spectral measures of $U_0$ and $U_\gamma$ (and of $U_{\gamma_1}$ and $U_{\gamma_2}$ for $\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2$) are mutually singular as scalar measures.

Problem. Develop a higher-rank ($d\ge 2$) analogue of Aronszajn–Donoghue theory for such families of finite-rank unitary perturbations. Specifically:

(a) Identify a suitable notion of "mutual singularity" for matrix/vector-valued measures that replaces scalar mutual singularity (which fails in general for $d\ge 2$, as simple direct-sum examples show).

(b) Determine which statements of classical Aronszajn–Donoghue theory — concerning the singular parts $M_{\gamma_1}^s$ and $M_{\gamma_2}^s$ for distinct parameters $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$, the absolutely continuous parts, and the relation between the perturbed and unperturbed operators — extend, after appropriate reformulation in terms of vector-valued measures, to the higher-rank unitary perturbation setting, and provide precise theorems with proofs.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on the higher-rank analogue of Aronszajn–Donoghue theory. A notion of vector mutual singularity for matrix-valued spectral measures has been introduced, and analogues of the singularity statement have been proved for finite-rank self-adjoint and unitary perturbations (Liaw–Treil and collaborators). Refinements such as the dimension of the exceptional set in the finite-rank Aronszajn–Donoghue theorem have also appeared (IMRN 2022). The full program of determining exactly which parts of the classical theory survive — and in what optimal form — remains an active area, so the broad open direction is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Matrix measures and finite rank perturbations of self-adjoint operators
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces vector mutual singularity for matrix-valued measures and proves an Aronszajn–Donoghue type theorem for finite rank perturbations.
status_evidence.claim: A matrix-valued analogue of Aronszajn–Donoghue mutual singularity has been established for finite-rank perturbations.

status_evidence.title: Dimension of the Exceptional Set in the Aronszajn–Donoghue Theorem for Finite Rank Perturbations
status_evidence.snippet: Refines the finite-rank Aronszajn–Donoghue theorem by analyzing the dimension of the exceptional parameter set.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative refinements of the higher-rank Aronszajn–Donoghue theory have been obtained.

status_evidence.title: Spectral Analysis, Model Theory and Applications of Finite-Rank Perturbations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of finite-rank unitary perturbations including matrix-valued Aronszajn–Donoghue results within Aleksandrov–Clark theory.
status_evidence.claim: Matrix-valued Aronszajn–Donoghue theory has been developed for unitary finite-rank perturbations.
